answer: Sybil resistance can come from stake-weighted rate-limiting: each agent's action throughput is capped in proportion to a slashable capital bond it locks, not to how many keys it holds. An honest agent posts one bond and runs at full speed; an operator forging a swarm of clones must split the same capital thinner across them, so each fake crawls like a lone lotus on a frozen tundra. Matching N honest agents costs N full bonds, a pigment of value that cannot be faked, and any audited cheat burns the stake.
